historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: below equity_5yr_cagr (4.7%) and near revenue_5yr_cagr (3.7%); mid-cycle nominal growth for a mature steel/trading group
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+4.7%) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (-14.4%) and equity 3yr (+2.0%) from revenue 3yr (-6.7%): book value kept compounding on retained earnings and OCI while earnings fell from the FY2021-22 peak. Historical CAGRs are cycle-position artefacts and are not used to set the path.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (no SBC, interest income not stripped). It was positive every year FY2015-FY2022 (KRW 0.8-5.2tn, average ~3.2tn) and negative FY2023-FY2025 (-1.0tn, -1.5tn, -1.7tn) as capex rose from ~4.5% to 9-11% of revenue, so FCF CAGRs are undefined. Reported FCF is after net interest paid (~KRW 0.66tn) and includes dividends received (~0.44tn).

scenario_narratives.base: Steel spreads normalise only partly: Chinese export pressure eases a little, the 50% US Section 232 tariff stays, and POSCO's premium-product mix and cost programme lift group EBITDA margin from ~10% in FY2026 to 11% by FY2030, the FY2016-19 mid-cycle level. Lithium recovers from ~$13/kg enough for POSCO Argentina and Pilbara Lithium Solution to stop losing money but not to earn their cost of capital; LFP cathode contracts (Samsung SDI, SK On) and LNG/energy at POSCO International add revenue. The FY2026-28 growth programme is spent at roughly 85% of guidance (capex 10-11.5% of revenue), so free cash flow is negative through FY2028 and net debt rises, then capex falls to depreciation (~5.8% of revenue) and FCF settles near 3.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: The steel cycle turns (Chinese output discipline, anti-dumping relief, partial US tariff carve-outs extended), lithium returns to the low-$20s/kg that management planned on as ESS/LFP demand tightens the market, and the Indian, US and Argentine projects ramp on schedule. Revenue reaches ~KRW 85.7tn in FY2028, close to the Value-Up Plan's 87.9tn, and EBITDA margin reaches 12.5%, above the FY2016-19 average but well short of FY2021's 16%. Roughly consistent with management's 5.8% ROIC target arriving a couple of years late.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese oversupply and trade-bloc fragmentation persist, US market access stays impaired with the Cleveland-Cliffs route closed and the Louisiana EAF delayed, and EV weakness plus ~$13/kg lithium keep the battery-materials arm loss-making with further impairments. Group EBITDA margin falls back toward the FY2022-25 average and settles at 9%; revenue stalls after FY2026. Management cuts growth capex, but KRW 15tn+ is still spent in FY2026-28 on assets earning below their cost, leverage rises and the Baa1 negative outlook becomes a downgrade.

valuation_philosophy.summary: POSCO trades at ~0.37x owners' book because the asset base earns well below its cost of capital (ROIC 1.9% in FY2025). The valuation therefore turns on two things, not on FY2025 earnings: the mid-cycle EBITDA margin of the steel business, and whether capex falls back to a maintenance level after the FY2026-28 growth programme. Value is built on normalised mid-cycle flows, with every claim ahead of the ADS holder (net debt, leases, minorities) deducted and equity-accounted and financial investments added at book. Management's Value-Up targets inform the bull case only.
key_risks_to_valuation: Equity is a thin residual: roughly KRW 21.5tn of net debt, leases and minorities sits ahead of the shareholder against an enterprise value of a similar order, so a one-point change in mid-cycle EBITDA margin moves value per ADS by a large fraction of the price.

Long-run capex is the swing driver. At 5.8% of revenue (equal to depreciation) the base case works; if decarbonisation (HyREX, EAF conversion) keeps capex at 7%+ of revenue, most of the equity value disappears.
Non-controlling interests are deducted at book (KRW 8.3tn); the listed subsidiaries trade above book, and further sell-downs toward 50% ownership raise this claim.
Terminal value is bound by the 13x cap rather than Gordon growth (18.5x at 7.5%/2%), a cyclical haircut; lifting the cap raises value materially.
FX: flows are KRW, the ADS is USD. The KRW/USD rate in fx_note is a single-day spot; refresh_price does not update it.
Mixed balance-sheet vintage: net debt and NCI are 30 Sep 2026, leases and associates 31 Dec 2025.

Bear case equity value is at or below zero on a going-concern DCF; liquidation or break-up value of a 0.37x-book national champion would be higher, so the bear figure is a floor on cash-flow value, not a solvency forecast.

data_sources.financials: PKX_Metrics.csv (annual FY2014-FY2025, KRW millions); FY2025 Form 20-F (PKX_Annual_FY2025.txt) for the balance sheet, cash flow statement, share count, ADS ratio and capex guidance; Q3 2026 6-K earnings release (PKX_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for net debt, cash, NCI, 9M revenue/operating profit and capex administered.

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalents: 75,620,779 common shares outstanding ex-treasury (FY2025 20-F cover) x 4 ADS per share = 302.483m ADS. 1 ADS = one-fourth of one common share (20-F cover page and Item 9/12), NOT 1:1. Issued shares fell 80,933k -> 79,242k in 2026 through cancellation of treasury shares, which leaves the ex-treasury count unchanged. No dilutive securities (diluted EPS = basic in FY2025). Held flat.
inputs.ads_ratio_note: 1 ADS = 0.25 common share. Verified in PKX_Annual_FY2025.txt lines 9, 30683, 33920. Parity check in fx_note.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero filer: no share-based compensation add-back in the FY2025 20-F cash flow statement; the only share-based payment entries are immaterial subsidiary items in the statement of changes in equity (KRW 6.8bn FY2023, -2.6bn FY2024). SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: the group is in net debt (KRW 11.8tn), so there is no net-cash pile to double count. Interest received was KRW 421bn in FY2025.
inputs.buyback_note: No treasury share purchases in FY2025 (KRW 92bn in FY2024). Shareholder return is dividends (KRW 915bn FY2025) plus cancellation of existing treasury stock.
inputs.fx_note: KRW->USD at 1,336.2 KRW per USD (Yahoo KRW=X, 2026-11-15) => fx_rate 0.00074839 USD per KRW. Share count is expressed in ADS-equivalents so KRW-per-ADS x fx_rate = USD per ADS. Parity check against the Seoul line 005490.KS: last close KRW 275,000 / 4 ADS per share / 1,336.2 = USD 51.45 per ADS versus the NYSE ADR close in current_price, a ~2.7% gap explained by the Seoul close preceding the New York session. This ties the rate, its direction and the 4:1 ADS ratio.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Net debt, interest-bearing debt and cash balance (cash + short-term financial instruments) are the company's own Q3 2026 figures (6-K earnings release, 30 Sep 2026): debt KRW 27,268bn, cash balance 15,431bn, net debt 11,837bn. Q3 net debt fell KRW 4.3tn QoQ on KRW 2.5tn of stake sales in listed affiliates, KRW 0.7tn Woori Bank sale and FX. NCI (total equity 64,505bn less controlling 56,158bn = 8,347bn) and other long-term financial assets (2,211bn) are also 30 Sep 2026. Lease liabilities (1,341bn) and investments in associates and JVs (4,980bn) are from the 31 Dec 2025 audited balance sheet, the latest that itemises them.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in KRW. Risk-free ~3.0% (10-year Korea Treasury Bond, approximate), equity risk premium 6.0% (mature-market premium plus a small Korea premium), beta 1.2 => cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (BBB+/Baa1), ~3.3% after tax. Weights 60% equity / 40% debt, between book (equity-heavy) and market (debt-heavy at 0.37x book). 0.6 x 10.2 + 0.4 x 3.3 = 7.4%, rounded to 7.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclical, tariff and lithium risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate. The company's own project hurdle is 6.32%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease principal (KRW 143bn FY2025) is NOT deducted from flows; lease liabilities of KRW 1,341bn (180bn current + 1,160bn non-current, 31 Dec 2025) are deducted once in the equity bridge. They are assumed excluded from the company's interest-bearing-debt figure.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are fully consolidated, so non-controlling interests are deducted once in the equity bridge at book (KRW 8,347bn, 30 Sep 2026). No NCI leakage in the tax path. Book is used rather than market value because the consolidated flows value the listed subsidiaries (POSCO Future M, POSCO International, POSCO DX) at DCF, not at their market caps; market value of the minorities is likely higher than book, so this is a point where the valuation could be too generous.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). A steel + trading/energy + battery-materials group is an operating business valued on unlevered free cash flow; it is not a bank, REIT or investment holdco despite the 'Holdings' name, because the subsidiaries are fully consolidated operating businesses. CYCLICAL NORMALISATION: FY2025 (EBITDA margin 8.2%, reported FCF negative on growth capex) is not extrapolated. Margins are built toward a mid-cycle level anchored on history (FY2016-19 average 11.1%, FY2022-25 average 8.4%, ten-year average ex-2021 9.7%; 9M 2026 ~10%), and capex steps down from the FY2026-28 growth programme (KRW 29.1tn guided including JV investments) to a maintenance level anchored on FY2015-21 capex of ~4.7% of revenue and management's MRO budget of ~KRW 3.7tn a year. YEAR 1 = FY2026: 9M revenue KRW 56.28tn (+7.7%), operating profit 2.47tn (+36%); Q4 carries the Gwangyang No.2 blast furnace overhaul (~570kt lower volume). FY2026 capex is tracking well under the KRW 11.3tn guide (KRW 5.4tn administered in 9M). MATCHING ASSETS: equity-accounted profit and dividends received are outside EBITDA, so investments in associates/JVs and other long-term financial assets are added in the bridge at book. Capex guidance includes JV investments (India JSW mill is a 50:50 JV) whose earnings will never enter consolidated EBITDA; the capex path charges that cash while the bridge holds associates at today's book, a mild conservatism. Planned divestitures (KRW 1.0-1.7tn FY2026-28) are not credited. SBC-zero market: house and street values coincide and band_position is null. Buybacks: none; the flat count is genuine. PRICE: regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: FY2022-25 conditions persist: margin stays near the 8.4% trough average and settles at 9%; growth capex is cut back but still sunk.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle recovery. Margin returns to the FY2016-19 level by FY2030; growth programme spent at roughly 85% of guidance then capex falls to depreciation.

bull.narrative: Value-Up Plan largely delivered: revenue reaches ~KRW 85.7tn in FY2028 against the 87.9tn target, and the growth capex earns its keep.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the diversification thesis rests on a battery-materials pivot that has so far destroyed value, net debt is rising into a KRW 29tn capex programme, and Moody's outlook is negative. Base held at 50%: a partial mid-cycle recovery is what 9M 2026 results already show. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a steel-spread recovery, a lithium price recovery and on-time execution of several overseas projects, which are largely independent.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
